coverageNote.note: SC Johnson operates ~70 manufacturing facilities across 40+ countries; ~10 in the US. We audited 10. International scope on request.

account.dossierIntro: SC Johnson runs the home cleaning, air care, and Ziploc network. 70 facilities; we audited 10. Fort Worth Regional DC runs 120 dock doors. Bay City MI is 400 acres of Ziploc manufacturing. 808 acres total. 3 of 10 sites are rail-served. YardFlow runs flammable-classified household trailers and standard CPG trailers on the same protocol with separate audit chains.
surprisingFindings: Bay City MI is 400 acres of Ziploc manufacturing. SC Johnson built the bag at scale.
Fort Worth runs 120 dock doors. SC Johnson's largest single-site distribution operation.
3 of 10 audited sites are rail-served. Home cleaning supplies ship primarily on truckload.

sites.name: Waxdale Plant - Mt. Pleasant WI

steps.step: Route to correct building / drop yard

sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster's supplied coordinate (42.712313, -87.885932) lands in open green
space at the north edge of the property — it is the geocode of the street
address, not the plant. Probing satellite outward (z14-z21) and corroborating
with the SC Johnson Waxdale Fact Sheet (the world's largest/fastest aerosol
plant, 2.2M sq ft, opened 1955) confirmed the facility: the very large
multi-building industrial campus immediately south of the supplied point,
bounded by a private entry boulevard on the north, 16th St on the south, a
wooded/wetland buffer on the west, and open land on the east. SC Johnson
signage ("SC Johnson — A Family Center") and SC Johnson's known on-site wind
turbines are both visible in Street View, confirming ownership. Locked center
at 42.70750, -87.88500 (centroid of the developed footprint).

fieldNotes.truckGate: Engineered multi-lane controlled entry at the head of the private north boulevard (~42.7121, -87.8860); white directional lane arrows split inbound/outbound around a central guard building.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Substantial central guardhouse with hipped roof, ~3-4 vehicle footprint, set in the median of the entry boulevard with traffic lanes routed around both sides. Larger than a typical booth but functions as the manned gate house.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide gate apron with multiple paved lanes and a deep boulevard approach; ample paved width to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Private boulevard from public road to gate and on to the docks is several hundred metres; easily holds 3+ trucks queued.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Multiple large trailer-storage lots in the north and mid-west of the campus, rows of nose-out parked trailers (white/blue/orange fleet) plus dock-adjacent banks; 50+ easily.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 2.2M sq ft, 15 production lines; multiple dock banks visible on separate building faces (NW bank and S/SE bank). Door count is an overhead-imagery estimate, banded 50+.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Distinct dock banks on different building faces (north-west building face vs south/south-east face) consistent with separated shipping and receiving.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus of ~9 distinct large buildings (manufacturing halls, warehouse, components plant, tank farm/dome) on one fenced property.
fieldNotes.railServed: Active rail spur curves into the property from the south-west with multiple sidings holding boxcars / covered hoppers.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale positively identified in the gate path; left false but listed uncertain — a scale could exist within the unmapped interior.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town industrial setting in Mt. Pleasant; large natural buffer (woods/wetland) on the west and open land around; broader setting judged Rural per rubric.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Perimeter box ~1.22 km N-S x 0.78 km E-W of fenced developed property; ~218 acres is an estimate of the active fenced footprint (SC Johnson land holding here is larger).

citations.claim: SC Johnson's official Waxdale fact sheet: largest global manufacturing facility, 2.2M sq ft, 15 finished-goods lines + components plant, owned/operated by SCJ in Mt. Pleasant, WI.
Jul-2025 local press: SCJ moving 170 jobs to a building near its active Waxdale manufacturing plant in Mt. Pleasant.
SCJ careers page actively recruiting Waxdale manufacturing roles; references its largest manufacturing facility.

verification.rationale: Three Tier-1 sources confirm current SCJ-operated production; divestiture/closure/WARN/idle gauntlet returned no credible negative.

sites.name: Bay City Plant (Ziploc) - Bay City MI
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster coordinate (43.619016, -83.872098) was a ROOFTOP geocode of 405
Marquette Dr and landed on the correct campus. Satellite probing (z14-z20)
plus the SC Johnson Bay City careers page confirmed the facility: a large,
mostly-fenced industrial campus on the east side of Bay City between the
residential grid and the Saginaw River. SC Johnson describes the site as
"more than 400 acres" with six production plants and ~400 team members
producing billions of Ziploc bags per year. Locked center at the developed
building cluster, 43.62050, -83.87050.

fieldNotes.truckGate: Large perimeter-fenced campus (chain-link fencing confirmed in Street View along the property edge). Buildings sit behind the fence with controlled access drives; classified as a gated site.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No manned guard booth positively identified at any entrance from available Street View; entrances appear to be fenced drives without a visible booth. Left false but flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Set true on the basis that a gated/fenced site with no visible guard booth implies kiosk / call-box / remote check-in. Medium confidence.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Internal campus roads run several hundred metres from public road to dock faces; ample queue depth.
fieldNotes.entryExitSeparate: Sprawling campus with multiple building access drives; inbound and outbound flows are not pinched through one common gate. Approximate call.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Large empty paved overflow/staging lots beside the warehouse leave abundant room for express-lane buildout.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Multiple dock banks across the warehouse and production buildings; trailers backed in observed on at least three building faces. ~45 doors estimated, banded 25-50.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Fan-pattern rows of parked trailers near the north warehouse and rows near the core production buildings; clear drop-yard activity, banded 25-50.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock activity on physically separate buildings (north warehouse vs core production cluster).
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: SC Johnson Bay City is a campus of ~6 production buildings plus warehouse, office and R&D structures on one ~400-acre property.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail lines run along the east edge of the property with rail-served lots adjacent; the campus footprint borders active rail. Rail service likely; flagged medium.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale identified; left false.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: SC Johnson states the Bay City site is more than 400 acres; much of it is undeveloped land. Perimeter box approximates the property; ~400 acres per company figure.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town Bay City setting with adjacent residential and farmland/open land; judged Rural per rubric (small-city industrial).

citations.claim: SCJ Bay City, MI site currently operates with ~400 team members across >400 acres / six plants producing billions of Ziploc bags annually; live open requisition.
Federal Circuit opinion dated Dec 30 2025 (Zip Top, Inc. v. SC Johnson & Son) treats SC Johnson as the current maker of Ziploc products, contradicting any completed divestiture.

verification.rationale: No evidence of any Ziploc/Home Storage sale or closure; SCJ careers page + active SC Johnson Home Storage LLC entity + Dec-2025 Federal Circuit case confirm SCJ still operates Bay City.

sites.name: South Side Soapbox Plant (method / Ecover) - Chicago IL
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster coordinate (41.696681, -87.601644) landed directly on the
distinctive method factory. Satellite probing and web research (Chicago
Neighborhood Development Awards, William McDonough + Partners, City of
Chicago) positively confirmed it: the "South Side Soapbox", method's first
U.S. manufacturing plant — a 150,000 sq ft LEED Platinum (first in the
cleaners industry, 85 points) soap factory in the historic Pullman district.
Two unmistakable signatures clinch the ID: a 230-ft on-site wind turbine
(visible in z20 imagery north of the building) and the Gotham Greens
75,000 sq ft rooftop greenhouse (the glass sawtooth roof section). Locked
center at 41.69700, -87.60160.

fieldNotes.truckGate: No barrier arm, sliding gate or checkpoint pinch-point observed. The truck driveway runs open from the public road into the dock yard; the building fronts open paved drives with no controlled entry. truckGate false.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth anywhere on the site. False.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False — there is no gate, so no remote check-in implied.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved truck yard north-east of the building provides interior holding space before the docks.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Open NE truck yard is deep — easily holds 3+ trucks staged.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Abundant unused paved width in the NE truck yard; ample room for any lane configuration.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Truck docks on the NE building face — a modest recessed dock bank with trailers backed in. ~16 doors estimated, banded 10-25.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Rows of parked trailers in the NE truck yard (some shared with adjacent Pullman-development buildings); banded 10-25 for the method-attributable portion.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Single dock bank on one building face; shipping and receiving not physically separated.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: One building (the 150,000 sq ft soap factory, which incorporates the Gotham Greens rooftop greenhouse). buildingCount 1.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail line runs along the west edge of the property but it is a through line / neighbor siding, not a spur into the method property. railServed false (flagged uncertain).
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Inside the City of Chicago (Pullman neighborhood); Urban despite the on-site restored prairie.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Per published facility data the site is 22 acres, of which only ~3.5 acres are developed (building + pavement) and the rest is restored natural prairie. Perimeter box approximates the developed/usable portion.

citations.claim: SCJ confirms it retains a manufacturing center in Chicago's Pullman neighborhood; the 2025 move relocates ~170 office roles to Wisconsin, not the plant.
SCJ Lifestyle Brands careers page for the Chicago South Side Soapbox at 720 E. 111 St.: active manufacturing/bottling/distribution for method and ecover (rooftop greenhouse, wind turbine).
Racine County EDC confirms manufacturing operations in Pullman remain active; relocated roles are office positions only.

verification.rationale: Multiple Tier-1 dated sources confirm SCJ-operated method/ecover Pullman plant active; the only 2025 event is an office relocation, plant stays open; no divestiture found.

fieldNotes.addressCorrection: Roster address '100 Technology Center Dr' is incorrect. Verified address is 1100 S Highway 27 (NC-27), Stanley, NC 28164 — the former Deb USA plant, now SC Johnson Professional USA (Waze, LoopNet APN 176716, FDA/Panjiva records). Roster coordinate (35.353526, -81.090317) was a city-centroid in downtown Stanley; corrected to the plant at ~35.3403, -81.0780.
fieldNotes.truckGate: No barrier arm, gate or checkpoint. The dock face fronts NC-27 directly with an open paved truck apron; trucks pull in straight off the highway. truckGate false.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth on the property. False.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False — no gate, so no remote check-in implied.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: The apron between NC-27 and the dock doors is shallow — room for only 1-2 trucks staged before the docks.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: The paved apron in front of the docks doubles as a small post-entry staging strip.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: A continuous bank of ~10-12 dock doors along the NE building face fronting NC-27, confirmed in Street View (red-trimmed dock wall with dock doors and trailers). Banded 10-25.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Only a handful of trailers parked on the apron / east side; no dedicated trailer-storage lot. Banded 0-10; dropYard false.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Single dock bank on one face. Raw materials likely received at the SW tank/silo area but no separate truck dock bank there; shipRcvSeparate false.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: One building (~73,956 sq ft, built 1986). buildingCount 1.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail line runs immediately along the west edge of the property; trailers/rail cars seen alongside the building's west face. Rail access likely but an in-property spur not definitively confirmed — flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Small-town Stanley, NC (Gaston County), surrounded by fields and woods; Rural per rubric.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Building ~73,956 sq ft; the fenced/paved operational parcel is small (~14 acres estimated from the perimeter box). Flagged uncertain.

citations.claim: Active SC Johnson Professional job openings in Stanley, NC as of June 2026.
Property record for 1100 S Highway 27, Stanley NC 28164 (73,956 sq ft industrial) — the audited address, occupied by SC Johnson Professional.

verification.rationale: SC Johnson Professional USA (ex-Deb USA) actively manufactures hand/floor care at 1100 S Hwy 27 Stanley NC; June-2026 job listings + property record confirm; no negative found.

sites.name: Fort Worth Regional Distribution Center - Fort Worth TX
sites.dossierExcerpt:
Roster coordinates 32.968943, -97.331494 (ROOFTOP geocode, moved 143 m) land
correctly on the building. Identity is supported by the **EPA Risk Management
Plan record** for the "Fort Worth Regional Distribution Center" and a Waze
listing ("DHL - SC Johnson"). The facility sits in the AllianceTexas
industrial area on the far north side of Fort Worth and is operated with DHL
Supply Chain. It is the dossier-noted Fort Worth RDC. Locked center
(per the JSON): 32.96895, -97.33145.

fieldNotes.truckGate: Truck driveways enter the site from the perimeter industrial road on the SW (Transport Dr side) and around the building with no barrier arm, sliding gate, or checkpoint. Street View (Sep 2025) of the truck roads shows wide-open paved driveways with no control. Open site.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth at any truck entrance. The dark elongated structure beside the SW driveway in z20 imagery is a parked trailer/container, not a guard booth.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Cross-dock building with continuous dock banks on both the east and west long faces - shipping and receiving run from physically separate dock clusters on opposite building faces.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Continuous bank of dock doors along both ~430m long faces; ~95 trailers backed in across the imagery, total doors well over 100 -> 50+ band.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Large paved drop yards flank both long faces with many trailers parked without tractors; capacity 50+.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Very wide paved truck yards and multiple wide open driveways - ample room for express/bypass lanes if a gate were added.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Open multi-tenant park roads; lane counts approximate from imagery.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Estimate from perimeter box covering the building and both truck yards; vacant land to the north excluded.

citations.claim: City of Haslet business directory lists 'S C Johnson (Exel)' at 850 Transport Drive, Haslet TX 76052 — SCJ occupier, Exel/DHL 3PL operator.

verification.rationale: Active Exel/DHL site for SCJ on the I-35W/Transport Dr corridor; no closure/WARN signal found, but the SCJ-client tie rests on an undated municipal directory (and a prior Shippers Warehouse tenant once shared the address) — PROBABLE, flagged, treat as moderate confidence.

fieldNotes.location: Confirmed via EPA RMP record (Carlisle Regional Distribution Center, 5 True Temper Dr) + Margulies Hoelzli Architecture project page + FCC ULS license 'EXEL SC JOHNSON' + LoopNet/FCC listings. 500,000 sq ft, 450 ft x 1,100 ft cross-dock built by First Industrial Realty Trust, tilt-wall, with local operations offices; operated with DHL/Exel. fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth at the entrance. A small office/operations annex sits at the NE corner of the building, not a road-side guard booth.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Cross-dock building (450x1,100 ft) with continuous dock banks on BOTH long faces (NW and SE), trailers backed in on both -> shipping and receiving run from physically separate dock clusters on opposite faces.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Continuous dock bank along both ~335m long faces of the cross-dock -> well over 100 doors -> 50+ band.

fieldNotes.entryExitSeparate: The wrap-around loop road allows distinct in and out routing at different points of the building perimeter.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Very wide truck aprons and the full wrap-around loop give ample room to add an express/bypass lane if a gate were installed.
